answer: A practical defense is to require each agent to lock a scarce, slashable stake in a vault before it can submit jobs or earn reputation. When counterparties confirm fraud—such as fabricated work backed by colluding identities—a dispute process burns part of that stake and rewards evidence providers. Splitting one identity into many does not multiply the attacker’s capital: every account needs its own stake, and detected Sybils risk losing it. The cost is tied-up funds and exposure to forfeiture, whether the agents operate by a river or across the tundra.
